rows.setType: If That Sounds Crazy...I Mean, You’Re Not Wrong. But The Same Was Also Said About The Regular 2025/26 NBA Chrome Sapphire Release At A $1500 Price Point. Right Before Zero People Scored It On EQL And It Was Instantly $3500-$4k/Box. It Also Just So Happened To Be One Of The Most Epic Products Of All-Time.
rows.setLine: If that sounds crazy...I mean, you’re not wrong. But the same was also said about the regular 2025 NBA Chrome Sapphire release at a $1500 price point. Right before zero people scored it on EQL and it was instantly $3500-$4k/box. It also just so happened to be one of the most epic products of all-time.

As with NBA Chrome Sapphire, every single auto in the product will be Gold or better. Auto checklists are also tighter than with regular NBA Chrome Update. There are not many checklist squatters included.
If you remember, with NBA Sapphire, odds on Purple parallels stated 1:22 packs. At this rate, they should have been numbered, and I believe that was the intention.

However, somewhere along the line this changed. Live product rips showed them inserted at an actual rate of 1:4 packs and they were numbered. Due to this, the parallel hit rate was an absurd 4.6 numbered cards/box.

As with NBA Chrome Sapphire, every single auto in the product will be Gold or better. Auto checklists are also tighter than with regular NBA Chrome Update. There are not many checklist squatters included.

rows.setLine: Caught in the Crossfire Chrome Base
Quality Hits are ~$161 ea. That’s surprisingly good. All Parallels are Yellow or better. So every single Parallel is considered a Quality Hit. And you’re getting basically 3.5-4 per box.

Now, there are “Base” Autos and Green Autos which I don’t love. I wish they would make more Auto Subsets like they do with NBA, WWE, & UFC Sapphire so no Autos are worse than Gold. They’re short-changing the MLB fans by not doing so. There is definitely plenty of room to make MLB Sapphire products better.
